name: core.openwop.workflows.exec-ops
description: Real-work workflow pack (RFC 0013, ADR 0149). The Executive / Chief-of-Staff cluster: Daily Executive Briefing, Meeting Prep & Attendee Dossier, and Board / Investor Update Pack. Reasons with core.ai.chatCompletion over real tenant data (feature.crm / feature.analytics) and, where a workflow touches an external system, binds a connection pack via core.openwop.http.openapi-call (connectionRef) — so a configured connection runs live and an unconfigured one surfaces a connect prompt rather than failing. Every external send is gated by core.chat.approvalGate; the read-only briefing is ungated. All tenant-specific values are run parameters (replay-deterministic). Resolves fully on hosts that ship the feature + http/mcp + chat packs (the OpenWOP reference app); the connection bindings are configured by the operator under Access & data → Connections.
author: openwop

chains.label: Daily Executive Briefing
chains.description: Synthesize a daily briefing from the pipeline, usage analytics, and open tasks: priorities, revenue deltas, risks, blockers, and next actions. Read-only digest — no external send, so no approval gate. Pair with a scheduled trigger (e.g. 06:30 local) registered by the operator.

orgId.description: The org whose pipeline + open tasks feed the briefing (feature.crm reads are org-scoped — an exact match against Deal.orgId/Task.orgId, so this MUST be set or the CRM reads are always empty).

provider.description: AI provider id for this chain's LLM nodes. Frozen into this chain's AI nodes when the workflow is created (ADR 0498 — a concrete provider is what keeps replay deterministic). Override at instantiation to use a different vendor or your own BYOK provider; whichever you pick, the workspace needs a key for it — the workflow will not fall back to another provider on its own.

model.description: Model id for this chain's LLM nodes. Must be advertised by `provider` in the host catalog; override at instantiation.

config.systemPrompt: You are a chief of staff. From the pipeline, usage analytics, and open tasks, produce a concise daily executive briefing emphasizing {{params.focusAreas}}: today's priorities, revenue deltas, risks, blockers, and recommended next actions.

chains.label: Meeting Prep & Attendee Dossier
chains.description: Ahead of a meeting, read the upcoming calendar events (whichever calendar the user connected — Google or Microsoft 365) and the attendee's company profile, then synthesize a dossier with an agenda and suggested objectives. Pair with a scheduled trigger N hours before the event.

orgId.description: The org the attendee's company belongs to. Must match the company's org exactly, or the company is not found.

attendeeCompanyId.description: The CRM company id of the meeting attendee/account.

meetingContext.description: Optional extra context about the meeting.

timeMin.description: ISO-8601 lower bound for calendar events (e.g. the scheduled trigger's fire time), so the read returns UPCOMING events. Empty lists by start order.

provider.description: AI provider id for this chain's LLM nodes. Frozen into this chain's AI nodes when the workflow is created (ADR 0498 — a concrete provider is what keeps replay deterministic). Override at instantiation to use a different vendor or your own BYOK provider; whichever you pick, the workspace needs a key for it — the workflow will not fall back to another provider on its own.

model.description: Model id for this chain's LLM nodes. Must be advertised by `provider` in the host catalog; override at instantiation.

config.systemPrompt: You are an executive assistant. Using the upcoming calendar event and the attendee company profile, write a meeting dossier: who/what/why, a proposed agenda, and 3 suggested objectives. Context: {{params.meetingContext}}

chains.label: Board / Investor Update Pack
chains.description: Assemble a monthly board/investor update: pull KPIs (analytics), pipeline (CRM), and finance figures (provider-agnostic ERP), draft a narrative with variance commentary, gate it for exec review, then deliver ONLY on approval — the distribute step takes its body from the gate on a `truthy approved` edge, so a rejected pack is not sent. Pair with a monthly scheduled trigger.

orgId.description: The org whose deal pipeline feeds the update. Must match the deals' org exactly, or the pipeline reads as empty.

provider.description: AI provider id for this chain's LLM nodes. Frozen into this chain's AI nodes when the workflow is created (ADR 0498 — a concrete provider is what keeps replay deterministic). Override at instantiation to use a different vendor or your own BYOK provider; whichever you pick, the workspace needs a key for it — the workflow will not fall back to another provider on its own.

model.description: Model id for this chain's LLM nodes. Must be advertised by `provider` in the host catalog; override at instantiation.

config.systemPrompt: You are a finance/strategy lead. For {{params.period}}, draft a board/investor update for {{params.audience}}: KPIs, pipeline, finance figures, narrative, and variance vs prior period with commentary.
